home.my_open_cases.title: My open cases
home.my_open_cases.text: Cases you own (you are the case owner) that are not closed. Owning a case also brings you the "Case you own is updated" notification when someone else edits its details.

home.my_open_alerts.title: My open alerts
home.my_open_alerts.text: Alerts you own whose status is not Closed, Merged or Escalated. Home looks at the 50 newest alerts you own (by event time) and counts the open ones among them; the Alerts page has the full list.

home.pending_tasks.title: My pending tasks
home.pending_tasks.text:
Case tasks you are an assignee of whose status is neither Done nor Canceled, in cases that are still open. Global tasks and war-room tasks are not included.

The menu on a row sets the task's status; Done or Canceled takes it off this list.

home.closed_30d.title: Closed in the last 30 days
home.closed_30d.text: Cases you own whose close date falls within the last 30 days.

home.my_reviews.title: My reviews
home.my_reviews.text: Cases that name you as reviewer and whose review status is neither Not reviewed nor Reviewed - in practice, reviews pending or in progress. The interface will not close a case that has no reviewer (the API does not check), and being named reviewer sends you the review-request notification.

home.current_case.title: Current case
home.current_case.text: The case you are working in, named by cid= in the page address; pages outside a case carry the last one along. These shortcuts, Add task log and the Case updates bell work on it; Switch case picks another one.

dashboard.import_case.title: Import case
dashboard.import_case.text:
Creates a new case from an .iris-case file made by Export in a case's information window, decrypted with the password chosen at export. Notes, IOCs, assets, tasks, evidence records and timeline events come across; evidence files, working-timeline rows, comments and saved AI results do not.

The customer and the lookup values are matched by name. A customer that does not exist here falls back to the first customer on this server, so check it after the import.

metrics.page.title: Metrics
metrics.page.text:
Figures computed live, each time the page loads, from every case on this server - not only the cases you can open. Cases of the IrisInitialClient bootstrap customer are left out of every figure.

Figures marked (range) follow the date range; (now) and (all cases) figures are current snapshots; the Case tagging and Sectors cards use a whole calendar year.

metrics.date_range.title: Metrics date range
metrics.date_range.text: The window for every figure marked (range): 7, 30 or 90 days back from today, the year to date, or two dates of your choice followed by Apply. Cases count by their open or close date, notes by creation date and logged time by the day it was logged for. Snapshot figures ignore it; the Case tagging and Sectors cards show the whole calendar year of its end date, and changing the range resets a year picked on those cards.

metrics.mttr.title: Median MTTR
metrics.mttr.text: Median time to resolve: over the cases closed within the date range, the middle value of close date minus open date, in days (a case opened and closed on the same day counts as 0). My median MTTR does the same over the cases you own.

metrics.untriaged_wt.title: Untriaged working-timeline rows
metrics.untriaged_wt.text: Rows imported into working timelines (Hayabusa, EZ Tools and the other import sources) that nobody has promoted to the case timeline or rejected yet, across every case, open or closed. The Working-timeline backlog table under Investigation quality lists the ten cases with the most.

metrics.your_activity.title: Your activity
metrics.your_activity.text: Your own figures: the cases you own and the work you did.

items.name: My open cases
items.text: Cases you own that are not closed.

items.name: My closed (range)
items.text: Cases you own that were closed within the date range.

items.name: My median MTTR
items.text: Median days from open to close over those cases.

items.name: My notes (range)
items.text: Case notes you created within the date range.

items.name: My working-timeline reviews (range)
items.text: Working-timeline rows you reviewed within the date range, counted by the status you gave them (promoted, rejected...).

metrics.team_throughput.title: Team throughput
metrics.team_throughput.text: How work moves through the whole team.

items.name: Cases opened vs closed
items.text: Per day within the date range: cases opened (by open date) and cases closed (by close date).

items.name: Classification mix
items.text: Every case by classification, whatever its state or dates; Unclassified means none is set.

items.name: Severity mix
items.text: Every case by severity, whatever its state or dates.

items.name: Top owners
items.text: The ten owners with the most cases opened within the date range.

items.name: Top customers
items.text: The ten customers with the most cases opened within the date range.

metrics.case_tagging.title: Case tagging
metrics.case_tagging.text: How cases are tagged, over a whole calendar year: the year of the date range's end, or the one picked on the card. Sector tags are left out because the Sectors card counts them, and tlp:* tags because nearly every case carries one, which would drown every other tag. Click the card to cycle through table, donut and multi-year bar views.

items.name: Tagged / Untagged cases (all time)
items.text: Cases with at least one remaining tag, and cases with none, over every year.

items.name: YTD top tag
items.text: The tag on the most cases opened in the chosen year.

items.name: Unique tags / applications
items.text: How many distinct tags are in use, and how many case-tag pairs they make, over every year.

items.name: Top case tag per quarter
items.text: The tag on the most cases opened in each quarter of the chosen year.

items.name: Cases by tag x quarter
items.text: The 15 tags on the most cases opened in the chosen year, counted per quarter.

metrics.sectors.title: Sectors
metrics.sectors.text: Cases per industry sector, over a whole calendar year: the year of the date range's end, or the one picked on the card. The sector comes from the case's sector tag (the DHS critical-infrastructure sectors and the other sectors of the catalog); a case with several sectors counts in each. Click the card to cycle through table, donut and multi-year bar views.

items.name: Tagged cases
items.text: Cases opened in the chosen year that carry a sector tag, out of all cases opened that year.

items.name: Missing sector tag
items.text: Cases opened in the chosen year with no sector tag.

items.name: YTD cases
items.text: All cases opened in the chosen year, with or without a sector tag.

items.name: YTD top sector
items.text: The sector with the most cases opened in the chosen year.

metrics.investigation_quality.title: Investigation quality
metrics.investigation_quality.text: Gaps in case work, across every case on the server (the date range does not apply).

items.name: Open cases missing notes/IOCs/assets/events
items.text: Open cases with no note, no IOC, no asset or no timeline event - one gap is enough. The red-flag table lists the 25 most recently opened.

items.name: Timeline events
items.text: Events on the case timelines of every case (working-timeline rows are not counted).

items.name: Events with cross-links
items.text: The share of timeline events linked to an asset, or to an IOC, whichever share is larger - a lower bound of the events with any link.

items.name: Working-timeline backlog
items.text: The ten cases with the most working-timeline rows still waiting for review.

metrics.time_tracking.title: Time tracking
metrics.time_tracking.text:
Time analysts logged on cases, in 15-minute steps, for days within the date range. The breakdown tables show the average time per case in each group - its total minutes divided by the number of its cases with time logged - so a customer with many cases does not dominate; CSV downloads the totals and the per-case figures.

Sector and incident type come from the case's sector tag and classification when the report is made; a case with several sectors counts in each.

overview.cases.title: Case queue
overview.cases.text:
The cases you can open, one page at a time: the open ones, or the closed ones too with Show closed. Each row shows the severity, the title, the SOC ID, the case number, the customer and the first tags, then the stage, the owner, the case's age and how long it has been idle. Click a row to see the case in the panel on the right; Open workspace opens the case.

The search box matches the title, the case number, the SOC ID, a tag or the customer. Filters builds a finer filter. The search, the filter, the sort and the page are kept in the address, so a link brings the same view back.

overview.kpis.title: Quick filters
overview.kpis.text: Counts over the open cases you can open, whatever filter is applied. Click one to show those cases:

items.name: Open
items.text: Every open case; clears the search and the filter.

items.name: Critical
items.text: Open cases whose severity is Critical.

items.name: Opened > 7d
items.text: Open cases opened more than seven days ago.

items.name: Assigned to me
items.text: Open cases you own.

overview.filter.title: Filter the queue
overview.filter.text: Add conditions on a case's fields - title, case ID, SOC ID, description, customer, severity, stage, classification, outcome, owner, opened by, reviewer, review status, tags, open and close dates, closing note. Match all of them (AND) or any of them (OR); a sub-group has its own AND / OR, so "severity is High AND (owner is me OR unassigned)" can be written. Text matches ignore case. Apply runs the filter; a condition without a value is left out.

overview.saved_filters.title: Saved filters
overview.saved_filters.text: Keeps the current filter, with the search and Show closed, under a name. A private filter is visible only to you; a public one to every user. Pick one to apply it; the address names it, so a link opens the queue with it. You can delete the filters you saved.

overview.idle.title: Age and idle
overview.idle.text: Age is the number of days since the case was opened. Idle is the number of days since the last activity in the case - any change to the case or to what it holds (notes, IOCs, assets, tasks, evidence, timeline), as the case's activity log records it; a case with no recorded activity counts from its open date. Idle turns orange after seven days. Sort by either one.

overview.stage_track.title: Stage track
overview.stage_track.text: Where the case is in its response: Open, Containment, Eradication, Recovery, Post-Incident, Reporting, Closed. With full access to the case, click a stage to move the case there - you are asked to confirm. Closing needs a reviewer on the case and asks for the closing note; moving a closed case to another stage reopens it. A case in a stage outside the track (such as In progress) shows its stage under the track.

custom_dashboards.page.title: Dashboards
custom_dashboards.page.text:
Dashboards of widgets you build yourself: figures, donuts, bars, lines and tables over cases, alerts, IOCs, assets, tasks, timeline events, evidence, notes and time entries. Each widget counts only what the person looking at it can open, so one shared dashboard shows each viewer their own figures. Cases and alerts of the IrisInitialClient test customer are left out of every figure.

The Statistics dashboard is built in: open it as it is, or clone it to change it. The Metrics page (Manage) stays as it was.

custom_dashboards.system.title: Built-in dashboards
custom_dashboards.system.text: Dashboards that come with IRIS. Nobody edits them; Clone makes a private copy you can change.

custom_dashboards.sharing.title: Shared dashboards
custom_dashboards.sharing.text:
A dashboard is private until its owner shares it. A shared dashboard is listed for every user, read-only: only its owner (and a server administrator) edits or deletes it, and anyone can clone it to customise a copy.

Sharing shares the layout, never the data: every viewer sees figures computed over the cases and alerts they can open.

custom_dashboards.filter_bar.title: Filter bar
custom_dashboards.filter_bar.text: Pickers shown above the dashboard - Customer, Case, Severity or Owner. A value picked there filters every widget whose source has that field; a widget whose source has none (Severity on IOCs, say) says so under its figure. The date range is always there.

custom_dashboards.source.title: Source
custom_dashboards.source.text: What a widget counts: cases, alerts, IOCs, assets, tasks, timeline events, evidence, notes or time entries. The dashboard's date range applies to each source's own date - a case's open date, an alert's creation time, the date an asset, an evidence item or a timeline event was added, a task's open date, a note's creation date, a time entry's day; IOCs follow their case's open date. A widget set to All time ignores the range.

items.name: Count
items.text: How many rows.

items.name: Count distinct
items.text: How many different values of a field (for example how many customers).

items.name: Sum / Average / Median / Minimum / Maximum
items.text: Of a number field: days open, days to close, minutes to detect, minutes logged, evidence size.

items.name: Share matching a filter
items.text: The percentage of the widget's rows that match a second filter - the false positive rate is the share of alerts whose resolution is False Positive.

items.name: List rows
items.text: A table of the rows themselves, with the columns you pick; the first column links to the row's case or alert.

custom_dashboards.group_by.title: Group by and split
custom_dashboards.group_by.text: Group by gives one bar, slice or point per value of a field. A date field groups by a time bucket - hour, day, week, month, quarter or year; Automatic picks one from the range. Rows without a value form the "(none)" group; groups beyond the limit can be summed as "Other". Split into series draws one series per value of a second field (bar and line charts). A row with several tags or assignees counts once in each of their groups.

custom_dashboards.thresholds.title: Thresholds
custom_dashboards.thresholds.text: For a number widget: colour the figure when it reaches a value (at least / at most). The first rule that matches wins; without one the figure takes the widget's colour.

custom_dashboards.json.title: JSON mode
custom_dashboards.json.text: The whole dashboard as JSON - name, description, sharing and the definition (sections, widgets, filter bar, the range it opens with). The server checks it as you type and lists what is wrong; switching back to Visual applies it once it is valid. View JSON on a dashboard shows the same text, ready to copy.

custom_dashboards.scope.title: Whose figures
custom_dashboards.scope.text: A widget counts only what the viewer can open: cases they have access to (and the IOCs, assets, tasks, events, evidence, notes and time entries of those cases), and alerts of the customers they belong to - every alert for a server administrator. The IrisInitialClient test customer counts for nobody: its cases, what they hold and its alerts are left out, and the customer and case lists never offer it. The preview shows your own figures; someone else opening the same dashboard can see different ones.

search.page.title: Search across cases
search.page.text: Searches every case on this server at once, whatever case you are in and whether or not you can open it; the search_across_cases permission is what gives you this page. Each search is written to the activity log with the term you searched. Results name the case and customer they come from.

search.scope.title: Search within
search.scope.text: Which kind of object to search, and which of its fields. % is a wildcard everywhere.

items.name: IOC
items.text: The exact IOC value, case-sensitive: add % for a partial match (%evil% finds every value containing evil). IOCs with no TLP set are not found.

items.name: Notes
items.text: Note content (not the title) containing the term, case-sensitive.

items.name: Comments
items.text: Comment text containing the term, case-sensitive.

items.name: Assets
items.text: Name, description, IP or domain containing the term, case-insensitive.

items.name: Tasks
items.text: Title or description containing the term, case-insensitive.

items.name: Evidence
items.text: File name, description or hash containing the term, case-insensitive.

items.name: Timeline events
items.text: Title, content or source containing the term, case-insensitive.

items.name: Cases
items.text: Name, description, SOC ID or closing note containing the term, case-insensitive.

activity.log.title: Activity log
activity.log.text: IRIS-NG's record of who did what: case objects created, edited and deleted, case updates, searches and more. The Activities page shows the newest 10,000 entries meant for display, from every case on the server and from none, and needs the activities_read (or all_activities_read) permission; Home shows the newest ten.

items.name: Manual input
items.text: Typed by a person with Add task log (in the header or the quick actions) and stored on the current case. Like every entry, it is saved with only its first letter upper-case.

items.name: From API
items.text: Made with an API key - a script or an n8n workflow - rather than from a browser session.

items.name: Quick actions, Activities tab
items.text: The current case's entries only; the blue ones came from the API.

activity.non_case.title: Show non case related activity
activity.non_case.text: Switches to the full log: it adds the entries normally hidden from activity views - sign-ins, failed sign-ins, MFA events, sign-outs, datastore downloads and the like. Up to 10,000 entries tied to a case plus up to 10,000 tied to none; those show the user's id number instead of a name. Needs the all_activities_read permission.

dim.tasks.title: DIM tasks
dim.tasks.text: The background jobs the workers have run, newest first: module hooks (enrichment, MISP sync and the other modules) and the other jobs IRIS-NG runs in the background; updater jobs are left out. This page lists up to 1,000, the Quick actions tab the latest 100. Click a task ID (in Quick actions, the module name) for its details and the module's logs.

items.name: State
items.text: The worker's state for the job. A tick means it ran to the end, which does not mean the module succeeded - open it to see Success; a cross means the job itself failed; a clock means pending, retrying or revoked. In Quick actions, green is a finished job and orange anything else.

items.name: Case
items.text: The case the module ran for, when the job carried one.

items.name: Processing module
items.text: The module and hook, for module jobs.

items.name: Initiating user
items.text: Who triggered the job; Shadow Iris when no user was recorded.

dim.module_verdict.title: Module result (Success)
dim.module_verdict.text: Success or Failure as reported by the module itself. It can say Failure while Task state says success: the job ran to the end, but the module reported a problem, and the Logs below say what. Task state is the worker's view of the job; this line is the module's.
